also: let me know what you are doing
let me know where you are

terms.gloss: to inform someone, give him information; certior fierī, to be informed
terms.grammar: phrase: certus in the comparative with faciō
evidence: Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.1.1: fac mē certiōrem
terms.comment: Latin gives information with a verb: fac mē certiōrem, let me know; certior factus sum, I have been told. The thing goes with dē.

terms.gloss: information given, a disclosure, a tip-off
evidence: Plaut. Cist. 4.2.9: facite indicium, sī quis vīdit (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ad. 4.4.7: id anus mihi indicium fēcit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Often of information laid against someone (Caes. BG 1.4).

terms.gloss: knowledge, finding out about a thing
evidence: M-O s.v. information: ūnicum fontem cognitiōnis nostrae, our only source of information (Sillig)

terms.gloss: an outline; an idea, a notion
evidence: Cic. ND 1.43: anteceptam animō reī quandam īnfōrmātiōnem
terms.comment: A false friend: classically a sketch (Vitruvius) or an idea formed in the mind. Morgan–Owens allows it for the act of informing (Thunberg 1784), not for information as facts.

terms.grammar: faciō with an ut-clause: “see to it that I know”; often the future faciēs or the imperative facitō
evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: sī quid acciderit novī, faciēs ut sciam
Traupman 102: facitō ut sciam; facitō ut sciam ubi sīs

phrases.latin: ut certiōrēs facerēmus absentīs, sī quid esset quod eōs scīre aut nostrā aut ipsōrum interesset
phrases.english: to tell those far away anything that it mattered to us, or to them, that they should know

phrases.latin: Item posthāc, sī quid opus erit, sī quid acciderit novī, faciēs ut sciam.
phrases.english: Likewise from now on, if anything is needed, if anything new happens, let me know.

phrases.latin: Tū mē velim certiōrem faciās, quid agās.
phrases.english: Please let me know what you are doing.

phrases.latin: Mē velim certiōrem faciās, quid agās.
phrases.english: Let me know what you are doing.
